(1) the C1P is characterized in polynomial time by a set of forbidden submatrices that can be computed from a given 0/1- matrix in polynomial time and (2) the C1-P is fixed-parameter tractable with respect to the number of rows and with respect to the sum of the number of rows plus the number of columns.

(1) we can approximate the Minimum Consecutive Ones Submatrix Problem (MCOP) within an approximation factor of (3/2) and (2) we can solve the Minimum Consecutive One Submatrix Problem (MOSP) and the Minimum Row/Column Consecutive Ones Subproblem within fixed-parameter tractable time.

the Consecutive Ones Submatrix Problem is (1) polynomial-time solvable if the number of columns is fixed, (2) approximable within a constant factor, and (3) approximable to within a factor that is arbitrarily close to one if the number of rows is fixed.

the C1P is not only a combinatorial property of matrices but also a property of the graph that is induced by the matrix's row and column indices.
